Four separate experiments were carried out using different quantities of $2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ hydrochloric acid and $2 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sodium hydroxide in insulated polystyrene cups.
After stirring, the maximum temperature was recorded and the results plotted on a graph as shown.
The temperatures of the acid and alkali on their own were also plotted on the graph. Two straight lines were drawn and extrapolated as shown.
What is the molar enthalpy change for the neutralisation reaction, in $ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$?
(Assume that the specific heat capacity of the solutions is $4 \text{ Jg}^{-1}\text{°C}^{-1}$, the density of dilute solutions is $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, and all heat is transferred to the solution.)
